notes:
SOURCE FOOTPRINT: exactly one implementation file, src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/chunk_reset/ChunkResetModule.java (234 lines), plus the standalone entrypoint src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/standalone/chunk_reset/ChunkResetStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_chunk_reset"), boots via StandaloneModuleBootstrap). No mixins (grep for "chunk" in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json returns nothing), no assets, no data files, no JEI plugin, no network packets, no DeferredRegister of any kind.

VERSIONS: `git log --follow` on the module file returns exactly one commit, 25db081 (2026-06-13), and `git describe --tags --contains 25db081` = v1.0.0-beta.2^0 — that commit IS the beta.2 tag. `git diff 25db081 -- <module dir>` is empty: the module has not been touched since. The STANDALONE JAR is younger: standalone/chunk_reset/ was added in 27c7405, first tagged v1.0.0-beta.23. build.gradle:406 lists `[ moduleId: 'chunk_reset', displayName: 'Vanilla Plus: Chunk Reset' ]` with no mixins/moduleDeps/dataGlobs. Bundle registration is unconditional at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:171.

CONFIG: constructor passes AbstractModuleConfig::createDefault → DefaultModuleConfig, which adds no buildModuleSpecificConfig. So the only keys are the framework-standard `enabled` + `debug_logging` (excluded from configKeys by convention). isEnabledByDefault() is not overridden → the Module interface default `true`.

NO LANG KEYS AT ALL. Every chat message is a hardcoded English Component.literal(...) (lines 90-125, 134, 152-156, 175, 190-197). Nothing is translatable; a doc page should not promise localisation. There is no chunk_reset key in en_us.json.

ENABLE GATE — DIFFERS BETWEEN BUNDLE AND STANDALONE JAR. onInitialize() (lines 53-56) registers the module on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS and logs "Chunk Reset module initialized - /chunkreset command ready!"; isModuleEnabled() is only consulted inside onRegisterCommands (lines 60-62).
  * BUNDLE: ModuleManager.initializeModules() (ModuleManager.java:83-114) builds `enabledModules` from ModulesConfig.isModuleEnabled(module) FIRST and calls module.initialize() only for those. A module disabled in the config at startup is therefore never initialized, never subscribes, and never logs that line. Turning it ON at runtime (`/vpa module enable chunk_reset`, a runtime override) CANNOT bring the command back — the subscription does not exist. Turning it OFF at runtime does take effect, but only the next time commands are re-registered (datapack reload / restart).
  * STANDALONE JAR: StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot() calls module.initialize() unconditionally (line 62; shouldInitialize() is not overridden), so the module always subscribes and the isModuleEnabled() check in onRegisterCommands is the only gate — there both directions work on the next command re-registration.

BUG — the pending reset does not remember the dimension. `pendingResets` is Map<UUID, PendingReset>, PendingReset = record(ChunkPos center, int radius) (lines 36-38, 85). executeConfirm applies those coordinates to `source.getLevel()` AT CONFIRM TIME (lines 138-144). Run /chunkreset in the Nether, step through a portal, click [✓ Confirm] → the Overworld chunks at the same ChunkPos get deleted. There is also no timeout and no cleanup on logout (in-memory HashMap only; the entry lives until confirm/cancel or a server restart), and a second /chunkreset silently REPLACES the pending entry via Map.put — only the most recent invocation can ever be confirmed.

DEAD GUARD — line 138 `if (!(source.getLevel() instanceof ServerLevel serverLevel))` can never fail: CommandSourceStack.getLevel() is declared `public ServerLevel getLevel()` in 1.21.1. The failure message "This command can only be used in a server level." is unreachable.

BUG — radius 0 always claims success. performReset counts `succeeded` (lines 180-185) but the radius == 0 branch prints the green "✓ Chunk [x, z] reset." unconditionally (lines 189-192); only the radius > 0 branch prints "finalSucceeded/total" (and even that keeps the green ✓ prefix on a partial failure). A single-chunk reset that failed in resetSingleChunk still reports success in chat; only the log has the error.

DOC CONTRADICTION — docs/modules/chunk_reset.md line 35 says "Per-chunk success/failure is logged." Only FAILURES are logged (getLogger().error at line 215). Successes produce no log line.

BIGGEST FUNCTIONAL LIMIT — nothing unloads the chunk, and a still-loaded chunk is written straight back. resetSingleChunk (201-218) does two things: level.setChunkForced(x, z, false), then reflectively invokes ChunkStorage's (ChunkPos, CompoundTag) method on the ChunkMap with a null tag. VERIFIED against the decompiled 1.21.1 sources the project compiles against: ChunkStorage.write(ChunkPos, CompoundTag) → IOWorker.store(pos, @Nullable tag) → RegionFileStorage.write, which does `if (chunkData == null) regionfile.clear(chunkPos)` — so a null tag really does clear the region-file entry. But ChunkMap.save(ChunkAccess) reaches the SAME this.write(chunkpos, compoundtag) (ChunkMap.java:792), so any chunk that is still loaded and unsaved gets re-written by the next autosave, silently undoing the deletion. The module neither forces an unload nor flushes, and does not warn about this. "It will regenerate when next loaded" therefore assumes the chunk actually unloads first — in practice: leave the area, or restart the server.

FORCE-TICKET REMOVAL IS VANILLA-ONLY. ServerLevel.setChunkForced(x, z, false) removes the position from ForcedChunksSavedData and calls ServerChunkCache.updateChunkForced — i.e. it only drops a vanilla /forceload ticket. NeoForge/mod chunk tickets (Create trains, this mod's own chunk_loader_rail/chunk_anchor, spawn chunks, a nearby player) are untouched and keep the chunk loaded → see the autosave note above.

TELEPORT IS NOT A SAFE-LANDING SEARCH (lines 169-178). Players whose chunkPosition() is in the target set are moved to x = center.getMiddleBlockX(), z = (center.z + radius) * 16.0 + 17.0, Y UNCHANGED (nearby.getY()), same level. That is one chunk beyond the +Z edge of the affected square, but with no ground/collision check — ServerPlayer.teleportTo(double,double,double) is a plain connection.teleport keeping rotation, so a player can end up inside terrain or in mid-air at the old Y. Only entries of level.players() are handled; mobs, item frames, item entities etc. in the chunks are simply destroyed with the chunk. Nothing stops a teleported player from walking straight back in — the chunk is still loaded.

REFLECTION DETAILS — resolveChunkStorageWriteMethod() (220-233) scans ChunkStorage.class.getDeclaredMethods() and takes the FIRST method whose parameters are exactly (ChunkPos, CompoundTag), setAccessible(true), caches it in a static volatile Method (unsynchronised, but the race is benign — both threads resolve the same Method). Deliberate, per the in-code comment, so the obfuscated/mapped name is not hardcoded. In 1.21.1 `write(ChunkPos, CompoundTag)` is the ONLY declared method with that parameter shape, so "first match" is deterministic there. ChunkMap extends ChunkStorage and does NOT override write, and ServerChunkCache.chunkMap is `public final` — so the plain field access at line 204 and the invoke at line 212 are both valid; no accessor mixin, no Mixin dependency at all. If no such method exists the code throws NoSuchMethodException, caught per chunk in resetSingleChunk and logged (then see the radius-0 false-success note above).

OTHER FACTS WORTH DOCUMENTING: permission level 4 (source.hasPermission(4), line 67) — ops only; .requires() on the root literal also covers the confirm/cancel subcommands. All three handlers call getPlayerOrException(), so console and command-block invocation always fails. MAX_RADIUS is a private static final int = 5 (line 39), NOT configurable — the 11x11 = 121-chunk ceiling can only be changed in code; the radius argument is IntegerArgumentType.integer(0, MAX_RADIUS) so out-of-range input is rejected by brigadier. The confirm/cancel chat buttons use ClickEvent.Action.RUN_COMMAND on "/chunkreset confirm" / "/chunkreset cancel" — a player can always type them instead. The command literal is "chunkreset" with no mod namespace, so it can clash with other chunk-management mods. The final success message uses sendSuccess(..., true) i.e. it is broadcast to other ops / logged as an admin action, while the warning prompt uses false.

REPO HYGIENE: README.md:299 still links the module doc as `docs/chunk_reset.md`, but the file now lives at `docs/modules/chunk_reset.md` (uncommitted working-tree rename at the time of this survey) — the link is stale, as are its siblings in that list. The README feature paragraph itself (README.md:156, "🗺️ Chunk Reset (command)") is accurate.

VERIFICATION BASIS: vanilla claims above were read from the decompiled 1.21.1 sources in the NeoGradle cache (~/.gradle/caches/ng_execute/<hash>/output, SharedConstants.VERSION_STRING = "1.21.1"), not from memory.

UNRESOLVED: Runtime behaviour was not observed — this is a read-only source survey with no gradle run and no server test. The autosave-undoes-the-deletion path is proven by reading vanilla 1.21.1 ChunkMap.save/IOWorker/RegionFileStorage, but has not been reproduced in game. Whether /reload (datapack reload) reliably re-fires RegisterCommandsEvent on NeoForge 21.1.x, which is what the enable-gate note assumes for 'takes effect on the next command re-registration'. Not provable from this repository.
oneLiner: An operator-only command that permanently deletes the chunk you're standing in — or up to an 11x11 square around you — so the world generator builds that terrain again from scratch, wiping every block, entity and structure in it.
shortDescription: Provides a command to delete and regenerate chunks from world generation
